notes:
Added
- Kirinuki can now ask your own Claude or ChatGPT account to pick the best moments of an episode. Connect it in the setup guide or in Settings → AI: Kirinuki downloads the official Claude Code or Codex program from its maker, checks that it is genuine, and you sign in on Anthropic's or OpenAI's own page. Kirinuki never sees your password or sign-in.
- Each AI pick says why it was chosen. Clips start on a cut, end after a sentence, last 40 to 60 seconds and stay clear of the opening and ending songs. Titles and descriptions never contain links or @names, and hashtags come only from your list.
- When your plan's limit is reached, the job waits and tells you when the limit resets, then carries on by itself. Without an AI account, or offline, Kirinuki still makes clips from the episode's sound, motion and speech and labels them "picked by signals only".
- Settings → AI shows your Claude allowance, the models you can choose (including ones that save allowance) and a list of recent AI runs.
- Kirinuki now recognises which series and episode a file is, from its name, and asks you to confirm when it isn't sure. You can change it at any time.
- Better captions for subtitled episodes: Kirinuki uses English subtitles from the file, from OpenSubtitles.com (with your own free account) or a translation by your AI account, and lines them up with the speech. For English dubs it keeps what the actors actually say. You can also pick your own subtitle file. Every job says which captions it used and why. Because OpenSubtitles' terms allow its subtitles for non-commercial use only, Kirinuki searches it on its own only when you turn that on in Settings → Captions; you can always search it for a single episode.
- Clips sound more even: each clip's sound is checked after encoding, so it lands on YouTube's loudness target with its peaks kept safely below clipping. Japanese captions now always use the bundled Noto Sans JP font.
- The licence list in About now includes anitopy and pysubs2, and a section for what Kirinuki downloads from its makers without shipping it: Claude Code, Codex and the anime id list from the Fribb anime-lists project.
